title: Perfect-algebra dual evaluation with its precomposition action
statement:
Let $q:S\to B$ be a map of commutative rings such that $B[0]$ is perfect over $S$, meaning represented by a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $S$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Work in ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with derived tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] and internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Put $E=C_q(S[0])\in D(B)$ using derived coinduction with precomposition action [def-trf-derived-coinduction], and let $\epsilon:E\to S[0]$ be its counit after restriction to $S$. For $V\in D(S)$ let $J_E(V)\in D(B)$ be derived $S$-linear Hom from $E$ to $V$ with precomposition $B$-action, as in [lem-trf-derived-bimodule-tensor-hom]: on a K-injective $S$-model $I$ it is $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(E^\bullet,I)$ with $(bh)(z)=h(bz)$. Define $\alpha_V:B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V\to J_E(V)$ to be the adjunct of
$$E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}(B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V)\cong E\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V\xrightarrow{\epsilon\otimes1}V.$$
Then $\alpha_V$ is an isomorphism in $D(B)$, natural in arbitrary $V\in D(S)$. After restriction to $S$ it is the perfect evaluation comparison $B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V\to R\operatorname{Hom}_S(E,V)$ induced by the canonical bidual map $B\to R\operatorname{Hom}_S(E,S)$. No flatness of $B$ over $S$, Noetherianity, or boundedness of $V$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $U:D(B)\to D(S)$ for restriction, $O=S[0]$, and $H(-,-)=R\operatorname{Hom}_S(-,-)$. By [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction], $UE=H(B,O)$ and the counit is evaluation at $1$. Apply [lem-trf-perfect-complex-derived-biduality] over $S$ to $B[0]$: $UE$ is perfect and the canonical bidual map $d:B[0]\to H(UE,O)$ is an isomorphism. We use the ordinary Koszul symmetry on module complexes. The additional braided-structure allowance in that node imposes no restriction here.

source.place: Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex; dualizing.tex Tags 0A70, lemma-right-adjoint, and 0A71, lemma-RHom-ext

proof.text:
For arbitrary $V$, [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the one-object ringed site gives a K-flat complex $F$ representing $V$. By [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] choose a K-injective resolution $O\to J$ and a K-injective resolution $q:F\otimes_S J\to I$. Thus $QI\cong V$. Choose any complex $M$ representing $UE$. Apply [lem-trf-perfect-source-evaluation-quasi-isomorphism] to $(M,F,J,I,q)$; its perfectness hypothesis holds by step 1. Its last displayed comparison, with $QJ=O$, is the canonical isomorphism
$$c_V:V\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}H(UE,O)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(UE,V).$$
The cited node fixes the arrow by its evaluation formula, including the unit comparison on the target. It applies to unbounded $F$ and $M$.

Form $\beta_V$ in $D(S)$ as
$$B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V\xrightarrow{\mathrm{swap}}V\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}B\xrightarrow{1\otimes d}V\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}H(UE,O)\xrightarrow{c_V}H(UE,V).$$
All three arrows are isomorphisms by steps 1--2. By the evaluation normalization of [lem-trf-perfect-source-evaluation-quasi-isomorphism] and the defining transpose of the canonical bidual map in [lem-trf-perfect-complex-derived-biduality], the transpose of $\beta_V$ is the pairing $UE\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V\to V$ obtained by tensoring $V$ with the usual evaluation $H(B,O)\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}B\to O$. Indeed uncurrying $c_V(1\otimes d)$ first evaluates $d(b)$ on $z$ and then multiplies $V$ by that scalar; by the bidual transpose this scalar is evaluation of $z$ on $b$. The swaps are precisely the Koszul symmetries in these transposes. No claim that a finite-projective $S$-representative carries a strict $B$-action is needed.

source.place: Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, canonical signed bidual evaluation; Tag 0BYN, lemma-internal-hom-diagonal-better, normalized evaluation

proof.text:
By [lem-trf-derived-bimodule-tensor-hom], the adjunct defining $\alpha_V$ exists in $D(B)$, has target $J_E(V)$ with the stated precomposition action, and its scalar restriction is the $S$-linear tensor-Hom transpose of its defining pairing. The pairing uses the action $UE\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}B\to UE$ followed by $\epsilon$ and then tensors $V$. By [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] and [def-trf-derived-coinduction], this first pairing is exactly usual evaluation: on the coinduced model $\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,J)$,
$$\epsilon(bz)=(bz)(1)=z(1b)=z(b).$$
This is an equality of the evaluation maps into the K-injective coefficient model $J$; pulling back along any resolution used to compute the derived tensor retains the equality. Consequently this is the same pairing as in step 3. The tensor-Hom bijection (also the case $S\to S$ of the cited bimodule adjunction) is injective, so $U\alpha_V=\beta_V$. This establishes the asserted comparison, rather than only existence of an isomorphism between its source and target.

source.place: Tags 09LN, lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction, and 09LT, lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint; dualizing.tex Tags 0A70 and 0A71, coinduction evaluation

proof.text: The defining pairing for $\alpha_V$ is natural in $V$: for $u:V\to W$, both pairing composites are $\epsilon\otimes u$ after the same tensor associator. Naturality of the adjunction of [lem-trf-derived-bimodule-tensor-hom] therefore gives $J_E(u)\alpha_V=\alpha_W(1_B\otimes u)$ for every derived morphism $u$, not merely for a chosen chain representative. By steps 3--4, $U\alpha_V$ is an isomorphism. Conservativity in [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] makes $\alpha_V$ an isomorphism in $D(B)$. The only finiteness used was the stated $S$-perfectness of $B[0]$; no flatness of $B/S$, boundedness of $V$, or Noetherian hypothesis entered.

That is V tensored with the bidual map, followed by the perfect-source evaluation for UE. I tested it on q=id, B=0, V=0 and S=Z, B=Z/p with V=Z and V=Z/p; the last gives the Tor_1 class in H^-1, so B need not be flat and V can be unbounded. Step 2: the K-flat F, the K-injective J and I, and F⊗J ≅ V by K-flatness meet the hypotheses of perfect-source-evaluation (QM perfect from step 1). Step 4: in the bimodule tensor-Hom node the counit is evaluation and J_E(V) is represented by Hom_S(E,I), so U(alpha) and beta have the same transpose pairing and are equal by injectivity. Step 5: naturality comes from the adjunction, and alpha is an isomorphism because the stated conservativity of U applies. Hypotheses are applied only to UE and B[0] over S; no flatness, Noetherian or boundedness assumption enters.
